parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The order-items validation appears in more than one place. Each copy is written out again rather than calling a shared definition.

1. CatalogueService.validateCombineItems copies the guard in OrderService.combineItems word for word: `if (!Array.isArray(items) || items.length === 0) throw new DomainError("An order requires at least one item")`. This also puts an order-placement rule inside the catalogue service, which owns product creation and listing, so the service mixes two concerns.

2. The candidate flags show that src/domain/order.ts:27 and :30 contain the same messages. So the domain Order already enforces "at least one item" and "positive integer quantity". OrderService.combineItems writes these invariants out again in the application layer instead of relying on the domain's own check.

Persistence is fine: both services reach storage only through the ProductRepository and OrderRepository ports. dtos.ts is cohesive. The failure comes from the duplicated validation and the order rule placed in the catalogue service.
